paragraphs: It is argued that advertising can have positive effects on economy while others argued that the negative social effects can outweigh the positive ones. There are strong cases to be made for both sides of the argument.

Admittedly, advertising bring undeniable economic benefits. This is predicted initially, on the assumption that due to creative content and appealing visual effects applied, it has stimulate consumer demand. More spending power would be increasing and also production is encouraged, leading to more employment opportunities and greater state revenues through taxation. For example, e-commerce platforms such as Shopee or Lazada in Vietnam rely heavily on advertising campaigns to attract customers.

On the other hand, advertising can have negative social consequences. Advertisements often show perfect lifestyles, beauty standards and expensive possessions. This can make people dissatisfied. Young people in particular may feel pressured to buy trendy clothes or the latest smartphones advertised on TikTok and Facebook. It creates the lead to frustration when they cannot afford items. Furthermore, advertisements may promote materialistic values and encourage a money-driven culture in the long run.
Overall, I strongly believe that both views are valid to a certain extent. Advertising can contribute to social dissatisfaction while playing a crucial role in economic development.

paragraphs: Advertising is often seen as an engine of economic development, whereas critics associate it with social dissatisfaction. There are strong cases to be made for both sides of the argument.

On the one hand, supporters of advertising often point to the undeniable economic benefits it can bring. When consumers spend more, firms can increase production, employ more workers and contribute more tax revenue. Online retailers such as Shopee and Lazada illustrate this effect by using campaigns to attract customers. Furthermore, advertising creates direct jobs for specialists in marketing, media and design. This process can benefit suppliers and services connected with online retail. It can also give consumers information about products they may need. This can make the economic benefit visible across the wider market.

Those on the other side of the debate, however, argue that advertising entails negative social consequences. Constant exposure to luxury possessions, ideal lifestyles and beauty standards can make viewers dissatisfied with what they have. Young people may then feel pressure to buy fashionable clothes or smart devices. If they lack the money for these products, frustration can follow and materialistic values may become stronger. Such repeated comparisons can influence how young consumers measure success. The effect is strongest when expensive products are presented as necessary.
In conclusion, advertising supports economic activity and employment. Nevertheless, it may also foster dissatisfaction and a money-driven culture.

paragraphs: The media play an significant role in people's lives today, while other argue that this influence is negative. Personally, I am the opposite school of thought.

It is true that the media have to much problems. With the wide spread access to smartphones and the internet, people can follow the news instantly wherever and whenever they are. News has become a regular part of their routine. Additionally, because of the intense competition among news outlets, most media agencies focus on shocking and breaking content. They use dramatic headlines and eye catching visual reinforced the overall impact of news on public opinion.

At the same time, the influence is not always bad. Constant exposure to a stream of distressing and exaggerated news can make people feel overly anxious and helpless, even when in situation do not directly affect them. However, news coverage also warn the public to existing and looming problems such as crime, natural disasters, or political corruption. For instance, when a typhone is reported on television, families in coastal areas can prepare by storing food and drink, securing their house. In this way, individual are better informed and more prepared to respond the risks in today's complex society.

In conclusion, the media have a important impact on people's lives. This can be negative [chưa đọc rõ] the news is too sensational but it also helps people stay informed and prepared. I partly agree, but I think the media are still necessary.

paragraphs: The media play a significant role in people's lives today, and some people argue that this influence is negative. Personally, I agree that this influence is considerable, although I do not consider it entirely negative.

It is true that the media have a considerable influence on people's lives. With the widespread access to smartphones and the Internet, people can follow the news instantly wherever and whenever they are. News has become a regular part of their routine. Additionally, owing to the intense competition among news outlets, most media agencies focus on shocking and breaking content. They use dramatic headlines and eye-catching visuals to reinforce the overall impact of news on public opinion.

At the same time, the influence is not always bad. Constant exposure to a stream of distressing and exaggerated news can make people feel overly anxious and helpless, even when the situations do not directly affect them. However, news coverage also warns the public to existing and looming problems such as crime, natural disasters, or political corruption. For instance, when a typhoon is reported on television, families in coastal areas can prepare by storing food and drink and securing their homes. In this way, individuals are better informed and more prepared to respond to the risks in today's complex society.

In conclusion, the media have an important impact on people's lives. This can be negative when the news is too sensational, yet news also helps people stay informed and prepared. I partly agree with the overall claim, although I think this influence also has clear benefits.

paragraphs: There is an opinion that all student who show best academic scores should be rewarded, other argue that the importance of rewarding improvemental students is necessary. Personally, I am sure that all kind of student should be rewarded.

Admittedly, It is true that students who have greatest academic results should be rewarded. Because diligent students are more often applied themselves to their studies, they deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage these students and other to study harder to win the rewards, help them propel towards overall academic gains. Additionally, this kind of competition seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individual are rewarded, make student use to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, enable them to achieve success in later life.

However, those who have improvements also should be rewarded. The rewards are only received by only a few smart students, cause others to think that their effort is futile. Because they can not surpass those outstanding individuals, proving to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened, and gradually losing the incentive to study. To emphasizing more improvement, school's rewards should encourage all students to be diligent in their studies and help students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves. Understanding how well they have been or are performing lead to the constant desire to outdo themselves even benefit themselves more than the competitive determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that those who have best scores and have improvement should be rewarded.

Tuy nhiên, Body 1 viết “students are more often applied themselves” sai khung động từ và dùng Because ngoài cách triển khai Cô yêu cầu; Body 2 ghép “The rewards are only received..., cause others...” sai cấu trúc, rồi chưa giải thích rõ sự tiến bộ giúp các em tiếp tục cố gắng như thế nào. Em cần viết lại hai thân bài với từng câu đầy đủ, giữ hai ý trong mỗi đoạn và giải thích được vì sao em dùng từng từ nối. paragraphs: There is an opinion that students who achieve the best academic results should be rewarded, while others argue that students who make progress should also be rewarded. Personally, I am sure that both groups of students should be rewarded.

Admittedly, it is true that students who have the best academic results should be rewarded. The first reason is that diligent students have applied themselves to their studies and deserve their praises and privileges. This may encourage these students and others to study harder to win the rewards. Their stronger motivation may improve the academic performance of the class. Additionally, this kind of competition is seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individuals are rewarded. This may help students become used to this reality and thrive in the face of fierce competition, which may enable them to achieve success in later life.

However, students who have made progress should also be rewarded. One reason is that if rewards are received by only a few high-achieving students, this may cause others to think that their effort is futile. They cannot surpass those outstanding individuals and may feel overwhelmed and disheartened, gradually losing the incentive to study. Furthermore, rewarding progress should encourage all students to be diligent in their studies and help students to understand that they need to constantly improve themselves. They can do so irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. The desire to outdo themselves may benefit them more than the determination to defeat others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that students with the best results and those who have made progress should be rewarded.

paragraphs: In some areas, parents are opting for teaching children themselves instead of sending them to school. Personally, I believe the disadvantages of homeschooling outweigh its advantages.

On the one hand, supporters of homeschooling argue that it has several benefits. First, it may help parents save money when they do not have to pay school fees. Moreover, home-educated students are less likely to experience bullying and peer pressure, which can cause emotional and mental problems. In addition, parents teaching their children at home by themselves can easily tailor their curriculum and pedagogical approaches to best suit their young ones, which is often not the case in traditional schooling due to large class sizes.

On the other hand, these apparent advantages may be outweighed by greater drawbacks. First, homeschooling may not actually save parents money: they may have to pay for laboratory equipment and tutors, and one parent may reduce paid work to meet their child's academic or personal needs, lowering household income. Additionally, most parents are not well-versed in every school subject; therefore, they may struggle to explain difficult concepts to their children, which can affect their academic progress. Finally, even social problems that children face at school, such as bullying or having romantic feelings for others, can help prepare them for social and workplace situations in the future.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that homeschooling has some advantages; however, its financial, academic and social disadvantages are more significant.
